candidates.story_title: House GOP blocks FY2027 NDAA procedural vote June 30, stalling Sullivan's $2.6B Alaska package
candidates.summary_2_sentences: Fourteen House Republicans voted 198-224 on June 30, 2026 to tank the procedural rule needed to bring the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act to the floor, forcing GOP leadership to cancel the week and adjourn for the July Fourth recess. The stall delays the broader NDAA that carries Senator Sullivan's 56 secured provisions and $2.6 billion in Alaska authorizations, including $15 million for resilient autonomous sensing in the Arctic and $10 million for autonomy within Golden Dome.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: Sullivan's package is the largest single-year defense authorization ever secured for Alaska and carries the Arctic autonomy and sensing money defense-tech firms plan around. Every week of delay extends authorization uncertainty for contractors at JBER, Eielson, and Fort Wainwright.
candidates.industry_consequence: Alaska defense sector: contractors and technology vendors face continued authorization uncertainty on the $2.6B FY2027 package, including autonomy and Arctic sensing lines, with the NDAA timeline now unclear beyond early July 2026.

candidates.story_title: Alaska LNG tax bill (HB 381) misses July 1 target; conference committee delayed to July 16, session expires July 19
candidates.summary_2_sentences: Alaska's conference committee on House Bill 381, the tax-relief package Glenfarne says is essential to the roughly $44 billion Alaska LNG pipeline, failed to produce a final draft by its informal July 1 target, with lawmakers not expected back in Juneau until July 16 and the special session set to expire July 19. Glenfarne President Adam Prestidge objected to a Senate amendment adding prevailing-wage and apprenticeship mandates beyond the June 11 union MOU, while a proposed corporate income tax on private developers that Governor Dunleavy has said he would veto remains the other unresolved issue.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: Every large-load data-center proposal pitched for the Railbelt or North Slope is premised on affordable North Slope gas arriving via the pipeline. A delayed or dead tax bill raises power-cost forecasts for any AI compute operator modeling a business case in Alaska.
candidates.industry_consequence: Energy and pipeline infrastructure: Glenfarne and AGDC face a July 19 session-expiry cliff; failure risks the developer's exit and cascading delays to gas-supply agreements, degrading the power-cost assumptions underwriting proposed AI data centers on the Railbelt.

candidates.story_title: DAF AI data-center lease RFLP (AFCEC-26-R-0006) closed June 29 at JBER, Eielson, Clear SFS; evaluation phase begins
candidates.summary_2_sentences: The Air Force Installation Contracting Agency's Request for Lease Proposals for commercial AI data centers across three Alaska installations reached its amended deadline of June 29, 2026 and moved to evaluation, with no award announced as of July 1. The best-value lease process now advances toward selection of one or more partners who would self-finance, build, and operate the facilities.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: The close is the pivot from marketing to selection for what would be Alaska's first large-scale private AI compute campuses on federal land. The outcome determines which operator enters the market and what utility, fiber, and workforce demands follow.
candidates.industry_consequence: AI infrastructure and defense real estate: AFICA now evaluates submissions; Railbelt utilities (Chugach Electric, GVEA) and broadband providers face a step-change in industrial load requests once a lessee is named.

candidates.story_title: Air Force Under Secretary Lohmeier tours JBER and Eielson, signals up to ~$8B Alaska investment over five years
candidates.summary_2_sentences: Under Secretary of the Air Force Matthew Lohmeier visited JBER and Eielson June 22-24, calling Alaska the crossroads of the Arctic and the Pacific and pointing to up to roughly $8 billion in projected Air Force investment in the state over the next five years. The visit coincided with the final week of the AI data-center lease-proposal window that closed June 29.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: An Under Secretary-level investment signal is the most explicit senior endorsement yet of Alaska as a multi-year federal capital destination, arriving the same week the data-center lease window closed.
candidates.industry_consequence: Defense infrastructure: base commanders have a live mandate to accommodate multi-year Air Force capex while the RFLP evaluation begins; utilities and contractors seeking site-prep or power-supply roles must engage the contracting office within the evaluation window.
candidates.softening_note: Air Force dollar figure appears as $8B and $7-8B and $11B FY27 request across sources. Attribute qualitatively to the Air Force / JBER commander, do not assert a precise number.

candidates.story_title: Dunleavy vetoes $16M in pipeline and vocational workforce training from FY2027 budget (June 24)
candidates.summary_2_sentences: Governor Dunleavy signed the FY2027 budget on June 24 while vetoing about $89.5 million total, including roughly $16 million across workforce-training facilities, among them AVTEC, the Alaska Teamsters construction driver training center, and the Fairbanks Pipeline Training Center. Senate Finance co-chair Bert Stedman tied the cuts to the gasline, saying the state is trying to push the project forward.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: The vetoed dollars were the state's down-payment on skilled-trades readiness for the Alaska LNG construction workforce, cut the same week the tax bill that would trigger that workforce stalled in conference.
candidates.industry_consequence: Energy and construction workforce: AVTEC, the Fairbanks Pipeline Training Center, and Teamsters training lose expansion funding, shrinking the in-state credentialed labor pool for pipeline preconstruction just as the LNG deal wobbles.
candidates.softening_note: Do not cite one exact training-cut line-item dollar unless verbatim-confirmed; $89.5M total is safe; $16M workforce grouping and named facilities are reported. Confirm Stedman quote verbatim before using.

candidates.story_title: Alaska AI-generated CSAM ban takes effect July 1 as part of omnibus crime package
candidates.summary_2_sentences: A new Alaska state law prohibiting the creation or possession of AI-generated child sexual abuse material took effect July 1, 2026 as part of an omnibus crime and public safety package sponsored by Rep. Sarah Vance. It creates state felony charges that let Alaska prosecutors act independent of federal law.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: It is the only Alaska AI-specific statute to cross the finish line this cycle, and it took effect the same week every AI economic-buildout decision stalled.
candidates.industry_consequence: Technology sector: Alaska-operating AI developers and platforms face new state criminal exposure for AI-generated CSAM effective July 1, 2026.
candidates.softening_note: Single-sourced (ADN). Verify the AI-generated CSAM provision and July 1 effective date appear on the fetched page. Use only as an in-passing contrast device, not a load-bearing claim, unless corroborated.

candidates.story_title: Alaska minimum wage rises to $14/hr July 1; exempt salary threshold climbs to $1,120/week
candidates.summary_2_sentences: Ballot Measure 1 drives a $1/hour minimum-wage increase to $14 effective July 1, 2026, with the exempt executive/administrative/professional salary threshold rising to $1,120 per week. State labor research chief Dan Robinson said market wages already exceed the floor in most sectors, so the direct effect is modest, but the higher exempt threshold forces payroll audits.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: For AI and technology employers scaling headcount, the revised exempt threshold is an immediate payroll-compliance deadline.
candidates.industry_consequence: Technology and professional services: employers with exempt staff between $1,040 and $1,120/week face a reclassification decision by July 1; the next step to $15/hr in July 2027 pushes the threshold to $1,200/week.

candidates.story_title: Workforce Pell Grants launch July 1 but Alaska published no eligibility framework, locking UA out
candidates.summary_2_sentences: The federal Workforce Pell Grant program opened July 1, 2026 for short-term certificate programs, but as of mid-June Alaska had published no governor-certified list of eligible programs and named no lead agency, placing it among states with no verifiable public action. University of Alaska short-term programs cannot receive Workforce Pell dollars until Governor Dunleavy certifies an eligible-occupations list.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: UA is the state's largest workforce-development provider, and the lockout lands the same week AVTEC's own expansion budget was vetoed, a double hit on the training pipeline.
candidates.industry_consequence: Higher education and vocational training: UA and AVTEC are locked out of Workforce Pell disbursements until the state certifies its list; competing states enroll and draw federal dollars this fall.
candidates.softening_note: Alaska 'no framework' status per Opportunity Data tracker as of mid-June; soften as 'as of late June, Alaska had not published' and attribute.

candidates.story_title: Alaska RHTP $272M application cycle closed June 22; AI-enabled healthcare grants expected Aug 1
candidates.summary_2_sentences: Alaska's application portal for the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program, distributing about $272 million in Year 1 federal funds, closed June 22 after advancing more than 400 projects, with AI-enabled tools and drone-supported delivery listed as eligible categories. Implementation grants are expected to be announced August 1, 2026.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: This is the largest single-year federal health capital deployment in Alaska history and will produce the state's first slate of publicly funded AI-healthcare deployments, the next real capital date after a week when nothing else closed.
candidates.industry_consequence: Rural and tribal healthcare technology: August 1 is the actionable date when the state names implementation-grant awardees from the $272M pool; named applicants include Tanana Chiefs Conference and Providence.

candidates.story_title: Alaska DNR extends STAK Energy North Slope data-center lease comment period to July 17
candidates.summary_2_sentences: The Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas posted an updated public notice extending the comment deadline on its preliminary best-interest finding for STAK Energy's proposed gas-powered HPC campus near the Dalton Highway from June 15 to July 17, 2026. DNR said the extension reflects public interest, not new applicant information, leaving the preliminary decision toward a 50-year lease unchanged.
candidates.why_it_matters_to_alaskans: The extension keeps a formal regulatory pathway open and signals DNR is proceeding methodically, pushing the earliest possible lease execution to late summer 2026.
candidates.industry_consequence: Oil-and-gas / data-center infrastructure: STAK's path to final lease execution now runs at least through late July, another buildout clock that slipped this week.
